newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in lethargic late trading on Friday.
Dealers said volume was thin in the dollar-rupiah market.
They said operators wanted to wait to observe central bank fixing policy on whether it would proceed with its depreciation policy it had pursued in the past two to three months.
Spot rupiah was at 2,361.50/62.00 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,361.80/62.30. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,361.55/61.90 and 2,361.25/61.50 respectively.
"There is no drive in the market. We hope the market will start normalising next week," one foreign bank dealer said.
The dealer said operators appeared bearish on dollars despite sustained ample rupiah supply in the market.
Another foreign bank dealer said speculation for a band widening seemd to have caused dollar selling, with many operators seen already factoring in this possibility.
One economist said, however, pressure on a band widening might diminish by itself as domestic interest rates were seen easing further, as reflected by weakening interbank rates.
He said further easing of local interest rates might help reduce the attractiveness of the rupiah against the dollar, and thus slowing down inflows of foreign capitals.
